lesson_title: Half a Doubling: The Secret of Fraction Powers
hook_text: Your video doubles its views every day. So what happened by lunchtime?
clip_script: Your clip doubles its views every single day. Day one: times two. Day two: times two squared. Day three: times two cubed. The exponent is just counting doublings. Now the question that breaks people's brains: what happened by LUNCHTIME — half a day in? Think about it. Whatever the lunchtime factor is, applying it twice has to finish one full doubling. So it's the number that squares to two. The square root of two. And we write it: two to the power one half. That's the entire secret of fraction powers. The bottom of the fraction says how many equal steps make one full multiplication. The top says how many steps you take. Eighty-one to the three quarters? Cut eighty-one into four equal multiplying steps — the fourth root, which is three — then take three steps: three, nine, twenty-seven. Bottom is the root. Top is the power. And that minus sign, like eight to the minus two thirds? It flips the answer upside down — one quarter — it never makes it negative. One warning before you go: the root of thirty-six plus sixty-four is the root of one hundred. Ten. Not six plus eight. Roots never split across a plus sign.
visual_style: A phone screen with a view counter racing upward, a day-night bar splitting in half at noon, then a number line of multiplying steps lighting up one by one as 81 breaks into four glowing threes.
pacing: Punchy through the doublings, a suspense beat on the lunchtime question, crisp on the rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make every fraction power read itself aloud.
